summary: slice(s) of pizza is what the Football Calorie (WC Edition) calculator works out, and it gets there from the I will have watched, the beer, the chips and the popcorn. It is built for a training session, a performance comparison or a competition result. The formula is printed further down, so you can check the answer by hand if you want to.

sections.title: How does the Football Calorie (WC Edition) calculator work?
sections.html:
The Football Calorie (WC Edition) calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports slice(s) of pizza in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the fat-burning activity); then you type in the I will have watched, the beer, the chips and the popcorn.

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• A number, expressed in matches.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in 500 ml. The unit chip switches it to any of the 14 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in 6 oz (170 g). The unit chip switches it to any of the 5 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in movie theatres size "small" (8 cups). The unit chip switches it to any of the 4 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in kilocalories. The unit chip switches it to any of the 33 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in kilocalories. The unit chip switches it to any of the 33 supported units.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 4 options, such as football, sex and running. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.

One field on this form is a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the Football Calorie (WC Edition) calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Slice(s) of pizza=-43 ÷ 27 × beer − 16 ÷ 27 × chips + (1 ÷ 270) × energy intake − 4 ÷ 27 × popcorn
My weight=(400 ÷ 987) × energy burned on cheering
Energy balance=I will have watched × (-energy burned on cheering + energy intake)
Energy balance=7700 × weight gain
Time needed to burn extra calories=(((weight gain < 0) ? ( 0 ) : ( (20 ÷ 21) × energy balance ÷ (fat-burning activity × my weight) )))

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Open the page and it is already filled in. With the values it starts from — I will have watched = 7, Beer = 2 large bottles, Chips = 1 medium bags and Popcorn = 0 small bags — it reports Energy intake = 0.332 kcal.

Those are real numbers produced by the same engine that runs when you press Calculate, so you can change any single box afterwards and watch the answer move from this starting point.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Energy intake = 0.332 kcal should be roughly the size you expected from I will have watched = 7 and Beer = 2 large bottles.

  • Shown in kilograms, and convertible to any of the 29 units on that chip.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • Beer container sizes, opening in 500 ml
  • Chips bag sizes, opening in 6 oz (170 g)
  • Popcorn size, opening in movie theatres size "small" (8 cups)
  • Pizza slice size, opening in medium pizza (12")
  • Energy, opening in kilocalories
  • Energy, opening in kilocalories
  • Energy, opening in kilocalories

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Football Calorie (WC Edition) calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Planning a session around a target you already know
  • Comparing two athletes or two attempts fairly
  • Tracking progress across a training block
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the I will have watched, the beer and the chips — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Football Calorie (WC Edition) calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns slice(s) of pizza, derived from the I will have watched, the beer and the chips. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Football Calorie (WC Edition) calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the I will have watched, the beer, the chips and the popcorn, which is 7 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter my weight in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. My weight opens in kilograms and the chip beside it offers 29 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There is one choice to make (1 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Energy intake = 0.332 kcal. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Football Calorie (WC Edition) calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
